script.title: Previous Year vs Assessment Year
script.caption_hook: Earned in 2025-26 but the Assessment Year says 2026-27? Here's why.

lines.say: Earned in 2025-26, but Assessment Year says 2026-27? Why?
Good question! You earn first, and tax comes later. The year you earn in is the Previous Year.
So what's the Assessment Year then?
The next year. Income of the Previous Year is taxed in the Assessment Year that follows.
Oh! So Previous Year first, Assessment Year after?
Yes! Priya earns salary from 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. That year is her Previous Year.
And when is she taxed on it?
In 2026-27, the Assessment Year, from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027.
Question says AY 2026-27. Which year's income do I take?
Go one year back. AY 2026-27 means PY 2025-26. Write both together.
Is the Previous Year always 1 April to 31 March?
Normally yes. For a new business, it starts on the setting-up date and ends on 31 March.

board.title: New business PY
lines: Starts: date it is set up

lines.say: Remember, Previous means Pehle. Earn in the Previous Year, pay in the Assessment Year.

check_notes: Writer: Removed the advance-tax/self-assessment board and the 'tax year' wording. Hook now says 'Assessment Year'. Word count about 165.

Checker: Line 13 voice and board ('Earn in PY, pay in AY!') and Line 2 ('tax comes later'): this is misleading. Much of the tax is actually paid during the Previous Year itself, through TDS on salary (Priya's case) and advance tax. The income is assessed and charged to tax in the AY. Suggested wording: 'Earn in the PY, get assessed in the AY.' If you keep 'pay', say 'the final tax is settled in the AY'.

Checker: Line 4 ('Income of the Previous Year is taxed in the Assessment Year that follows'): this is fine as the general rule, but add 'as a general rule'. There are exceptions where income is taxed in the same year it is earned: shipping business of non-residents, persons leaving India, AOP/BOI formed for a particular event, persons likely to transfer property to avoid tax, and discontinued business.

Checker: Line 12: the new-PY rule applies to a newly set-up business or profession and to a new source of income. Suggested wording: 'For a newly set-up business or profession, or a new source of income, the PY starts on the date of setting up, or the date the new source comes into existence, and ends on 31 March.'
